What readers learn:
- Treat repeated attention, language, habits, and choices as directions that gradually shape identity and behavior.
- Notice when a stated desire and a practiced inner direction move in opposite ways.
- Recognize fear, resentment, distraction, and old stories as patterns that can be rehearsed without conscious choice.
- Use morning orientation, midday correction, and evening review to interrupt inherited momentum.
- Realign through small credible actions rather than dramatic declarations or perfection.
- Hold personal responsibility without pretending that illness, injustice, tragedy, or loss are self-created.
- Use reflection to identify old agreements, hidden loyalties, and values the calendar does not support.
- Translate insight into a repeatable thirty-day practice of attention, boundaries, honest language, and intentional action.

Audience: For readers drawn to reflective self-help, mindfulness, habit change, journaling, and intentional living who want a structured way to connect inner attention with visible daily choices without reducing life to simplistic positive-thinking formulas.

### Do the Thing

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/do-the-thing/
- Language: English
- Category: Self-Help & Productivity
- Subtitle: Why Preparation Feels Like Progress—and How to Finally Act
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=BsTZEQAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=BsTZEQAAQBAJ&hl=en

Do the Thing studies the distance between preparing for a life and changing it through action. It begins with respectable forms of delay: cleaner systems, more research, better tools, improved plans, public intentions, and endless readiness. It distinguishes support work from state-changing work and follows the psychology of almost through undefined goals, fear of exposure, identity built around delay, and the comfort of remaining in potential rather than contacting reality. Action is treated as the mechanism that produces feedback, reduces ambiguity, rewrites identity, and teaches the body that beginning can be survived. The middle sections develop an action psychology built around starting before certainty, finishing small things, letting clarity emerge after movement, treating motivation as a result, and using repeatable wins. The later action system becomes concrete: define one real next step, design the first ten minutes, remove friction, use cues and calendars, create bounded time containers, finish open loops, handle emotionally difficult tasks, recover quickly after interruption, and collect evidence instead of hype. The long game closes on private progress, resistance from others, self-respect through kept commitments, and a life built by what was actually done.

Key topics: Procrastination; Preparation versus progress; False motion; Research as refuge; Fear of exposure; Identity and delay; Action before certainty; Feedback and clarity; Finishing and completion; Motivation after movement; Small repeatable steps; First-ten-minutes method; Friction design; Time containers; Emotionally difficult action; Recovery after interruption; Evidence over hype; Private progress; Self-respect and kept commitments

What readers learn:
- Distinguish real progress from planning, research, optimization, and organizational work that never changes the external state.
- Recognize how fear of exposure and attachment to potential keep a project safely imaginary.
- Use small experiments and contact with reality to generate feedback, clarity, and confidence.
- Begin before feeling ready and treat motivation as something that often follows engagement.
- Lower the threshold of action through tiny repeatable steps, first-ten-minute rituals, cues, and reduced friction.
- Use bounded time containers and clear definitions of done to reduce open loops and increase completion.
- Recover quickly after interruption instead of turning every lapse into a ceremonial restart.
- Replace public identity claims with private evidence, kept commitments, and work that can be verified.

Audience: For writers, creators, founders, students, professionals, and chronic over-preparers who are active around their goals but repeatedly delay the exposed, imperfect, reality-changing actions that would move the work forward.

### 0DTE Options: Trading the Same-Day Market

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/0dte-options/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: A Practical Guide to Same-Day Options, Greeks, Market Structure, Execution, Risk Control, and High-Speed Decision-Making
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=QJ0MEgAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=QJ0MEgAAQBAJ&hl=en

0DTE Options: Trading the Same-Day Market explains how same-day expiration compresses option mechanics, market movement, execution risk and behavioral pressure into a very short decision horizon. The first part builds the language of 0DTE and the Greeks; the middle converts those mechanics into structures and market contexts; the final part integrates execution, risk, evidence and trader behavior rather than treating them as separate subjects.

The book emphasizes that the shortest expiration does not simplify trading—it removes time that might otherwise hide weak decisions. Hypothetical examples are presented as educational mechanics rather than expected returns, while changing contract specifications, settlement conventions, trading hours and broker rules are flagged for verification. Reusable appendices support preparation, execution and post-session review.

Key topics: 0DTE options; Same-day expiration; Option Greeks; Market structure; Options execution; Risk control; Trade structures; Expiration mechanics; Decision-making; Session review

What readers learn:
- Understand the mechanics and Greeks that become especially important as expiration approaches within the same day.
- Connect option structures to underlying market context instead of evaluating contracts in isolation.
- Account for rapid changes in execution quality, spread, slippage and decision speed.
- Build risk controls appropriate to premium loss and strategy-specific exposure.
- Use repeatable pre-session, live-session and post-session review tools rather than improvising under time pressure.

Audience: For options traders who want a structured introduction to same-day expiration, including mechanics, execution and risk rather than a collection of high-speed trade calls.

### AI-Assisted Crypto Futures

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/ai-assisted-crypto-futures/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: The Smart Three-Screenshot Method for Multi-Timeframe Futures Trading
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=nzniEQAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=nzniEQAAQBAJ&hl=en

AI-Assisted Crypto Futures builds a disciplined workflow around three clean screenshots: 1H for direction, 15M for the working zone and 5M for timing. Screenshots are treated as evidence rather than decoration, so each one must show the timeframe, recent swing points, active price area and enough history for the AI assistant to evaluate whether price is extended, balanced or structurally unclear. The prompt must ask for visible evidence, invalidation, risk and a reason to stand aside.

The book combines multi-timeframe analysis with market structure, liquidity sweeps, Fair Value Gaps, funding awareness, trend and range filters, stop audits, position sizing, take-profit checks and no-trade defenses. It repeatedly emphasizes modest leverage, isolated margin, fixed stop-loss logic and capital protection. AI is one structured input inside the risk process, not a gambling voice or a substitute for the trader's written plan and final execution decision.

Key topics: AI-assisted futures; Crypto futures; Three-screenshot method; 1H / 15M / 5M analysis; Market structure; Liquidity sweeps; Fair Value Gaps; Position sizing; Leverage discipline; No-trade rules

What readers learn:
- Use a three-screen hierarchy with 1H for direction, 15M for the working zone and 5M for execution timing.
- Capture screenshots that contain enough visible evidence for analysis instead of forcing the model to guess from the last candle.
- Prompt for invalidation, position size, target realism, conflict and explicit reasons not to trade.
- Integrate structure, liquidity, FVGs, funding and volatility without turning any single concept into permission to enter.
- Keep leverage, margin mode, stops and capital protection inside the same written process as AI-assisted analysis.

Audience: For crypto futures beginners and developing traders who want to use AI as a structured chart-review assistant while keeping risk, leverage and execution decisions under human control.

### Beyond the Single Candle

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/beyond-the-single-candle/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: A Visual Field Guide to Inside Bars, Engulfing Patterns, and Two-Candle Price Action
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=ndIKEgAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=ndIKEgAAQBAJ&hl=en

Beyond the Single Candle moves away from memorizing isolated candlestick names and studies what changes from Candle 1 to Candle 2. Range, body and close location are kept as separate dimensions so an Inside Bar, body engulfing pattern or Outside Bar has a mechanical definition before context is interpreted. Compression is treated as an observable condition, not a directional prediction.

Mother-bar breaks, close confirmation, break-and-retest entries, false breakouts and engulfing relationships are compared with their different information costs. No-trade rules, invalidation and context are defined with the same precision as entry conditions. A two-candle worksheet and personal playbook encourage the reader to record facts, assumptions and risk before revealing the outcome, making the framework suitable for replay and testing.

Key topics: Two-candle price action; Inside Bars; Engulfing patterns; Outside Bars; Compression; Mother-bar breakout; False breakouts; Close location; Invalidation; Trading playbook

What readers learn:
- Describe the relationship between two candles before reaching for a pattern name.
- Keep range, body and close location as separate pieces of evidence.
- Define strict Inside Bars, engulfing patterns and Outside Bars consistently.
- Compare breakout, close-confirmation and break-retest entry styles with explicit invalidation.
- Use worksheets and versioned rules to test false breaks and two-candle setups without hindsight.

Audience: For candlestick and price-action traders who want to replace pattern memorization with a more precise, testable reading of two-candle relationships.

### Breaker Block Trading

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/breaker-block-trading/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: A Rule-Based Guide to Failed Order Blocks, Structural Transitions, Entries, Risk, and Testing
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=w-oMEgAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=w-oMEgAAQBAJ&hl=en

Breaker Block Trading begins where an earlier order-block thesis fails. Instead of treating a breaker as another rectangle to memorize, the book focuses on the event sequence: the prior expectation, the failure, displacement, structural change, retest, invalidation and objective. It compares breaker blocks with order blocks and mitigation blocks, then adds Fair Value Gaps, liquidity sweeps, premium/discount and dealing-range location.

Higher-, middle- and lower-timeframe charts are assigned different jobs—context, location and execution—so the trader reads a chain of evidence rather than a pile of contradictory signals. Entry models, stops, targets, trending and ranging markets, session context, low-quality setups, failures, checklists, case studies, testing and a final playbook turn breaker terminology into a falsifiable process.

Key topics: Breaker blocks; Failed order blocks; Displacement; Liquidity sweeps; Fair Value Gaps; Premium and discount; Multi-timeframe mapping; Entry models; Invalidation; Backtesting

What readers learn:
- Identify the failed thesis that creates a breaker instead of starting from a rectangle.
- Differentiate breaker blocks from order blocks and mitigation blocks.
- Use liquidity, displacement, FVGs and premium/discount as contextual evidence.
- Assign context, location and execution roles across timeframes.
- Build entries, invalidation, targets, testing and journaling around explicit breaker rules.

Audience: For SMC and ICT-style traders who already know order blocks and want a deeper, rule-based framework for failed zones and structural transitions.

### BREAKOUT & RETEST TRADING

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/breakout-and-retest-trading/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: Breakout and Retest: A Rules-Based Trading Strategy
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=SycOEgAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=SycOEgAAQBAJ&hl=en

Breakout & Retest Trading organizes the strategy into a fixed chain: context, level, break, acceptance, retest, trigger, invalidation, target space, risk and execution. The book begins by defining meaningful levels and distinguishing a real break from a brief penetration, then studies closes, acceptance, follow-through, volume, overextension and the quality of the return to the broken area.

Role reversal, entry triggers, stop placement, target space, false breakouts, news, session and volatility context are converted into a rules engine rather than a pattern slogan. Grading, risk limits, backtesting, journaling, case studies and no-trade branches make the framework useful for both execution and review.

Key topics: Breakouts; Retests; Acceptance; Role reversal; Entry triggers; False breakouts; Volume; Session context; Risk management; Backtesting

What readers learn:
- Select levels that matter before a breakout occurs.
- Distinguish a break from acceptance and define what a valid retest must do.
- Use trigger, invalidation and target space as separate parts of the setup.
- Filter overextension, news, session and volatility conditions that reduce trade quality.
- Grade and backtest the complete sequence rather than cherry-picking clean retests.

Audience: For traders who use support, resistance and breakout structures and want a repeatable breakout-and-retest process with explicit confirmation and risk rules.

### Candlestick Patterns From Zero

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/candlestick-patterns-from-zero/
- Language: English

Candlestick Patterns From Zero is a 100-page visual course that teaches candlestick reading from basic OHLC anatomy through pattern recognition, market context, confirmation and risk-aware execution. The book treats candle patterns as clues rather than guarantees: readers learn to interpret bodies and wicks, bullish and bearish candles, doji structures, hammers, shooting stars, engulfing patterns, harami patterns, morning and evening stars, multi-candle formations and gaps while checking trend, support and resistance, volume, volatility and higher-level context. Later lessons connect recognition to practical decision rules for entry triggers, stop-loss placement, targets, risk-reward, invalidation and confirmation.

Key topics: Candlestick anatomy; OHLC; Body and wick psychology; Doji; Hammer and inverted hammer; Shooting star and hanging man; Engulfing patterns; Harami patterns; Morning and evening stars; Multi-candle patterns; Market context; Confirmation; Entry triggers; Stop-loss placement; Targets; Risk-reward; Invalidation

What readers learn:

- Recognize common bullish, bearish and neutral candlestick formations without treating them as automatic signals.
- Judge patterns in relation to trend, support and resistance, volume, volatility and market location.
- Wait for confirmation and define an entry trigger instead of entering solely because a pattern appears.
- Place stops beyond logical invalidation points and map targets from chart structure.
- Evaluate risk-reward and know when a technically attractive pattern is still a poor trade.
- Use a confirmation ladder and reliability checklist to turn pattern literacy into a repeatable process.

### CHoCH & BOS

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/choch-and-bos/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: Reading Market Structure Shifts
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=7SIPEgAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=7SIPEgAAQBAJ&hl=en

CHoCH & BOS: Reading Market Structure Shifts turns two heavily used trading labels into observable, testable structural events. Rather than calling every opposite candle a Change of Character or every broken high a Break of Structure, the book begins with swing selection, pivot stability, candidate versus confirmed pivots, structural hierarchy, protected references, and the prior state that a continuation break is supposed to continue.

The book treats CHoCH as a meaningful structural violation that can move the market into transition without guaranteeing an immediate reversal, while BOS is evaluated against an already defined directional state. Context is allowed to filter a decision but not rewrite whether an event occurred after the outcome is known. Invalidation comes before targets, entry trigger is separated from entry location, failed events remain in the journal, and no-trade is treated as a legitimate system decision rather than an absence of analysis.

Key topics: CHoCH; BOS; Swing selection; Structural hierarchy; Protected swings; Transition states; Continuation; Invalidation; Context filters; Trading journal

What readers learn:
- Choose and confirm meaningful swings before applying CHoCH or BOS labels.
- Distinguish continuation structure from transition and reversal hypotheses.
- Keep event classification separate from later context and outcome so the method remains testable.
- Define invalidation, entry location, and trigger before focusing on targets.
- Journal failed breaks and no-trade decisions instead of editing history around winners.

Audience: For SMC, ICT and price-action traders who use CHoCH and BOS and want clearer definitions, less hindsight labeling, and a more reproducible structure-reading process.

### Confluence Trading

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/confluence-trading/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: A Visual Practical Guide to Combining Price Action, Market Structure, Key Levels, Multiple Timeframes, and Risk

- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=RS0LEgAAQBAJ&hl=en

Confluence Trading treats confluence as a way to organize evidence, not a score that makes uncertainty disappear. The early chapters distinguish independent evidence from duplicate evidence and put market structure and location before indicators. Key levels, price action, support and resistance, Fibonacci, moving averages, momentum, volume and multiple timeframes are evaluated according to what new information they add rather than how many boxes they allow the trader to tick.

The later sections turn analysis into a trade thesis with a separate trigger, invalidation and risk budget. Conflicting evidence can reduce or cancel a setup, and risk is allowed to veto a visually beautiful chart. Trend pullback, breakout/retest, reversal and range-bound setups lead into hidden-right-edge exercises, a personal confluence playbook, backtest logs, pre-trade and post-trade worksheets and a visual appendix.

Key topics: Confluence trading; Independent evidence; Market structure; Key levels; Price action; Multiple timeframes; Fibonacci; Moving averages; Invalidation; Risk management

What readers learn:
- Distinguish independent evidence from multiple indicators that repeat the same information.
- Put structure and location before confluence counting.
- Use Fibonacci, moving averages, momentum and volume as context only when they add distinct evidence.
- Separate thesis, trigger, invalidation and risk instead of treating confluence as an entry by itself.
- Build and test a personal confluence playbook with worksheets and outcome-independent process grading.

Audience: For discretionary traders who combine several technical tools and want to reduce duplicate evidence, confirmation shopping and false confidence.

Bright clusters are treated as conditional stress zones rather than guaranteed magnets or future price targets.

The book develops a full trading workflow around cluster distance, density, open interest, funding, volume and CVD, market structure, cascades, continuation and reversal hypotheses. - Build risk-controlled setups with explicit invalidation, sizing, journaling and review.

### Fair Value Gaps

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/fair-value-gaps/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: A Rule-Based Guide to Imbalance, Structure, Liquidity, Entries, Failure, and Testing
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=YNMLEgAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=YNMLEgAAQBAJ&hl=en

Fair Value Gaps begins with exact three-candle geometry so the concept is defined before interpretation. A gap is identified from the relationship between the first and third candles, while displacement, gap size, volatility, spread, slippage and economic significance are treated as separate filters. The book warns against retrospective adjectives such as clean or institutional unless their properties were specified before the next candle printed.

Market structure and liquidity sweeps are then layered around the FVG, with swing definitions stated explicitly so confirmation cannot move with hindsight. Inverse Fair Value Gaps are introduced as failed prior expectations rather than automatic role reversals. Measurable rules, invalidation, no-trade cases and testing are used to turn a popular visual concept into a reproducible research and execution framework.

Key topics: Fair Value Gaps; Three-candle imbalance; Displacement; Gap size; Market structure; Liquidity sweeps; Inverse FVG; Invalidation; Trading costs; Backtesting

What readers learn:
- Define bullish and bearish FVG geometry objectively before adding discretionary filters.
- Measure gap size relative to price, ticks or volatility instead of judging only by visual width.
- Connect FVGs to explicitly defined structure and liquidity events.
- Treat an iFVG as a new hypothesis after failure, not an automatic opposite signal.
- Write measurable filters before outcome so backtesting remains reproducible.

Audience: For SMC, ICT and price-action traders who want a stricter definition of Fair Value Gaps and a method that can be tested before outcomes are known.

### FALSE BREAKOUTS / FAKEOUTS:

False Breakouts / Fakeouts turns the familiar idea of a failed breakout into an operational sequence that can be recorded before the result is known. The book distinguishes the reference boundary, penetration, acceptance outside the level, reclaim, confirmation and invalidation so a wick beyond support or resistance is not automatically labeled manipulation or reversal.

Structure, liquidity, time, session context and execution are then used to decide whether a failed break deserves a trade, a watchlist entry or rejection. The framework emphasizes measurable rules, risk, journaling and testing so attractive completed charts do not quietly redefine what counted as a fakeout after the fact.

- Define invalidation and risk before choosing a target.
- Test fakeout rules on failed and no-trade cases as well as attractive reversals.

The New York AM window receives the deepest teaching focus, not as a claim of universally superior performance but as a controlled laboratory. Inducement Trading defines IDM as a conspicuous internal price reference that may carry clustered orders before price reaches a deeper point of interest, while carefully treating that interpretation as a hypothesis rather than proof of hidden institutional intent. The book establishes higher-timeframe context, dealing ranges, liquidity, protected swings and independent POI selection before asking whether a visible level is a plausible inducement.

The execution sequence then moves from sweep to response: reclaim, CHoCH or MSS, displacement, entry, invalidation, position sizing and structural targets. - Define structural invalidation, execution risk and target before placing an order.

### Inverse Fair Value Gaps (iFVG)

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/inverse-fair-value-gaps-ifvg/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: Inverse Fair Value Gap Trading
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=vtoMEgAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=vtoMEgAAQBAJ&hl=en

Inverse Fair Value Gaps (iFVG) starts with ordinary Fair Value Gap geometry and asks what changes when the original imbalance loses its role and price establishes itself on the opposite side. The useful information is the failed expectation, not merely a rectangle changing color. The book defines bullish and bearish iFVGs, then connects inversion to market structure, liquidity sweeps, displacement, premium/discount and dealing-range location.

Multi-timeframe analysis leads into three practical entry models, stops, invalidation, targets, risk and confluence without indicator overload. Four market environments, false iFVGs, failure modes, backtesting, a complete process and eight case studies keep the framework testable. FVG, iFVG, MSS and BOS are treated as practitioner terms whose exact conventions must be stated rather than assumed universal.

Key topics: Inverse Fair Value Gaps; Fair Value Gap anatomy; Market structure; Liquidity sweeps; Displacement; Premium and discount; Multi-timeframe analysis; Entry models; Failure modes; Backtesting

What readers learn:
- Define ordinary FVG geometry before deciding whether an imbalance has truly inverted.
- Read an iFVG as a failed prior expectation plus new observable price behavior.
- Combine iFVGs with structure, liquidity, displacement and premium/discount without treating confluence as certainty.
- Compare three entry models with explicit stops, invalidation, targets and risk.
- Backtest false iFVGs and failure modes as carefully as successful examples.

Audience: For SMC and ICT-style traders who already understand basic FVGs and want a structured approach to inversion, execution and failure analysis.

### Liquidity Sweep:

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/liquidity-sweep/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: A Practical Guide to Stop Runs, False Breakouts, Market Structure, Trade Confirmation, and Risk-Controlled Execution
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=gDkLEgAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=gDkLEgAAQBAJ&hl=en

Liquidity Sweep treats liquidity first as a visible location problem rather than a claim about invisible actors. Prior highs and lows, equal levels, previous-day and previous-week extremes, session boundaries and range edges are marked before price arrives. A sweep is then classified by what price actually does—penetration, reclaim, acceptance, continuation or structural response—rather than by an assumed stop-hunt narrative.

The book explicitly rejects the idea that taking liquidity must cause reversal. Strong trends can consume one local pool and continue toward a larger external objective, and volatile or fragmented markets can print venue-specific extremes. Entry confirmation, invalidation, targets, risk, XAUUSD and index examples, market-specific considerations, bullish and bearish casebooks, journaling and replay convert the concept into a decision process that can retain failures and no-trade cases.

Key topics: Liquidity sweeps; Stop runs; False breakouts; Previous-day liquidity; Session liquidity; Reclaim; Continuation sweeps; Market structure; Confirmation; Risk-controlled execution

What readers learn:
- Map visible liquidity references before the sweep occurs.
- Distinguish sweep, grab, breakout, reclaim, acceptance and continuation by observable behavior.
- Use structural response and confirmation before assuming a reversal.
- Account for session, venue, volatility and leverage differences across markets.
- Plan invalidation, target, risk and journal evidence before judging the outcome.

Audience: For price-action, SMC, forex, futures and crypto traders who use liquidity language and want a testable distinction between a level being crossed and a tradable reversal actually forming.

### MACD Trading Mastery

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/macd-trading-mastery/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: A Seven-Book Master Collection for MACD Foundations, Histogram, Crossovers, Divergence, Trend Following, Multi-Timeframe Analysis & Confluence
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=oJvdEQAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=oJvdEQAAQBAJ&hl=en

MACD Trading Mastery is a seven-part master collection built to move the reader beyond the familiar habit of treating MACD as a traffic light. The collection brings together MACD Foundations; MACD Histogram Trading; MACD Crossovers & Zero-Line Trading; MACD Divergence Trading; MACD Trend Following; Multi-Timeframe MACD; and MACD Confluence. Across the full sequence, the indicator is treated as a mathematical transformation of price that must be interpreted inside market structure, regime, timeframe and risk rather than as a stand-alone prediction engine.

The opening material develops the mechanics of the MACD line, signal line, histogram and zero line, then separates trend from momentum and shows why price should be read before the indicator. The histogram volume focuses on acceleration and deceleration before a crossover. The crossover and zero-line material reframes late signals as context-aware evidence rather than automatic entries. The divergence section covers regular, hidden and structural divergence without turning every disagreement between price and momentum into a reversal forecast. Trend-following chapters examine bull and bear markets with momentum confirmation, while the multi-timeframe framework assigns distinct jobs to Daily, 4H, 1H, 15-minute and 5-minute charts so lower-timeframe noise cannot casually overrule higher-timeframe context.

The final confluence volume connects MACD with RSI, Bollinger Bands, Supertrend, Ichimoku, Stochastic and ATR while warning against false confidence created by stacking indicators that are often derived from the same price data. Throughout the collection, readers encounter chart-reading protocols, observation journals, alignment matrices, checklists, historical or clearly labeled schematic figures, and explicit invalidation logic. The practical goal is not to make MACD infallible. It is to make interpretation more accountable: describe what the calculation actually supports, identify what remains uncertain, decide what evidence would change the thesis, and keep position sizing and risk independent from indicator enthusiasm.

Key topics: MACD foundations; MACD line and signal line; MACD histogram; Zero-line analysis; Crossovers; Momentum acceleration and deceleration; Trend versus momentum; Regular hidden and structural divergence; Trend following; Market regimes; Daily 4H 1H 15m and 5m analysis; Multi-timeframe alignment and conflict; RSI confluence; Bollinger Bands; Supertrend; Ichimoku; Stochastic; ATR; Observation journals; Invalidation and risk control

What readers learn:
- Explain what MACD is measuring instead of reacting mechanically to colors, crossovers or histogram bars.
- Read price structure first and use MACD as a second layer of evidence rather than a substitute for the chart.
- Interpret histogram expansion and contraction as changes in the relationship between the MACD and signal lines.
- Distinguish descriptive crossover evidence from an automatic buy-or-sell command and use the zero line as context rather than certainty.
- Separate regular, hidden and structural divergence and test whether price structure actually confirms the momentum story.
- Use MACD in bull, bear, range and transition regimes without assuming one setting or signal has the same meaning everywhere.
- Assign different jobs to Daily, 4H, 1H, 15-minute and 5-minute charts so higher-timeframe context, setup and execution remain logically separated.
- Combine MACD with RSI, Bollinger Bands, Supertrend, Ichimoku, Stochastic and ATR without mistaking correlated indicators for independent confirmation.
- Build an observation journal, alignment matrix, checklist and invalidation process that can be recorded before the outcome is known.
- Keep position size, risk and the option to wait or take no trade independent from indicator enthusiasm.

Audience: For stock, futures, forex, commodity and crypto traders who already recognize MACD on a chart but want a much deeper, structured understanding of momentum, trend, divergence, multi-timeframe analysis and confluence. It is especially useful for discretionary traders who want to replace crossover-only thinking with a repeatable chart-reading and risk-management process.

Mastering Renko Trading presents Renko as a visual framework for filtering some time-based chart noise and studying price movement through brick construction. The book focuses on reading trends, organizing entries, managing risk and turning Renko observations into rules that can be tested rather than treating the cleaner chart as automatic proof of a better strategy.

Its practical orientation connects visual pattern recognition to entry planning, stop logic, position risk and strategy validation. The central goal is to use Renko deliberately as a transformed view of price while keeping the trading process explicit enough to review and improve.

Key topics: Renko charts; Renko bricks; Trend reading; Noise filtering; Entry planning; Invalidation; Risk management; Strategy testing

What readers learn:
- Understand Renko as a transformed visual representation rather than a replacement for disciplined execution.
- Read trend and price movement with less dependence on ordinary time-based candle noise.
- Translate Renko observations into explicit entry and invalidation rules.
- Plan position risk rather than relying on visual cleanliness.
- Test Renko strategies with repeatable definitions before drawing performance conclusions.

Audience: For technical traders who want a practical visual introduction to Renko charts with explicit attention to entries, risk and testing.

### Mastering Support & Resistance

Mastering Support & Resistance is designed as an 80-page visual field guide for turning vague horizontal lines into usable trading decisions. It teaches the reader to identify a meaningful level, convert the line into a realistic zone, wait for price behavior at that area and enter only when the planned confirmation and invalidation logic are present. The book treats support and resistance as maps of probability rather than guaranteed predictions.

The visual lessons cover bounces, entries, exits, breakouts, retests, failed breaks and traps with candlestick examples, support and resistance zones, supply and demand context, liquidity references, checklists and risk reminders. Its practical emphasis is on reading reaction first, separating a level from a signal and making the trade plan clear enough that patience, confirmation and risk can override the temptation to buy or sell blindly at a line.

- Distinguish bounces, breakouts, retests and fake-breakout traps.
- Define invalidation, exits and risk alongside the level instead of after entering.
- Use visual checklists and chart examples to build a repeatable support-and-resistance process.

### Multi-Timeframe Analysis

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/multi-timeframe-analysis/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: Multi-Timeframe Trading: From Bias to Entry
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=1OsMEgAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=1OsMEgAAQBAJ&hl=en

Multi-Timeframe Analysis treats top-down trading as a decision architecture rather than a ritual of opening several charts. Its deliberate sequence is regime, context, bias, location, setup, trigger, invalidation, target and management. Each timeframe is assigned a job so contradictory information can be described rather than resolved by simply choosing the chart that supports the desired trade.

The book moves from higher-timeframe context into execution while preserving the distinction between historical evidence and schematic examples. Role-based models for scalping, intraday and swing trading show how the same architecture changes with holding period, while failure analysis, testing and journaling address the places where multi-timeframe reasoning becomes hindsight or confirmation shopping.

Key topics: Multi-timeframe analysis; Market regime; Directional bias; Location; Setup and trigger; Invalidation; Trade management; Scalping; Intraday trading; Swing trading

What readers learn:
- Assign a distinct analytical job to each timeframe instead of collecting directional votes.
- Move from regime and context to bias, location, setup and trigger in a fixed order.
- Define invalidation, target and management before lower-timeframe detail overwhelms the thesis.
- Adapt the framework for scalping, intraday and swing trading.
- Test and journal timeframe conflicts and failures without confusing profit with process quality.

Audience: For discretionary traders who use multiple charts and want a clear hierarchy from higher-timeframe context to lower-timeframe execution.

### Order Blocks Trading

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/order-blocks-trading/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: A Practical Guide to Finding, Validating, Refining, and Trading High-Probability Price Zones
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=9UILEgAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=9UILEgAAQBAJ&hl=en

Order Blocks Trading presents the order-block idea as an operational price-action method rather than proof of private bank or institutional inventory. The identification sequence is deliberately strict: choose the governing timeframe, mark relevant liquidity, identify displacement, confirm structural consequence, trace the move to its origin, check freshness, and define invalidation before considering an entry. Starting from the rectangle and searching backward for reasons is treated as confirmation bias.

Bullish and bearish blocks, liquidity before the block, quality filters, refinement and multiple entry models are developed with visual, rule-based examples. A liquidity sweep inside the block can become a local execution event only when subsequent displacement and structure provide the required confirmation. Stops, targets, position risk, reconstructed case studies and backtesting keep the method accountable to rules that existed before the outcome.

Key topics: Order Blocks; Displacement; Market structure; Liquidity sweeps; Zone freshness; Refinement; Entry models; Invalidation; Position sizing; Backtesting

What readers learn:
- Identify order blocks from context, displacement and structural consequence rather than by drawing rectangles first.
- Use liquidity and freshness as filters without claiming knowledge of hidden institutional inventory.
- Refine zones only after the governing timeframe and invalidation are clear.
- Compare entry models including confirmation and liquidity-sweep sequences inside the block.
- Backtest blocks with the same qualification and risk rules used in live analysis.

Audience: For SMC and price-action traders who want to replace subjective order-block drawing with a defined sequence for qualification, execution and review.

Premium & Discount Zones treats premium and discount as relative coordinates inside a deliberately chosen dealing range, not as automatic buy and sell instructions. The book explains equilibrium, range selection, structural context, liquidity, displacement, and the difference between price being low in a range and a bullish trade actually being justified. It repeatedly separates location from direction so a discount zone is never confused with proof that price must rise.

The framework then becomes multi-timeframe and executable: higher-timeframe location defines the question while lower-timeframe structure can refine timing without casually rewriting the original premise. Nested dealing ranges, liquidity sweeps, displacement, invalidation, entry planning, risk, and the danger of microscope bias are organized into a process for finding cleaner asymmetry without turning a midpoint or rectangle into a prediction engine.

Key topics: Premium and discount zones; Dealing ranges; Equilibrium; Market structure; Liquidity; Displacement; Nested timeframes; Entry planning; Invalidation; Risk control

What readers learn:
- Define a dealing range before labeling price as premium, discount, or equilibrium.
- Separate relative location from directional structure and trade confirmation.
- Use liquidity, displacement, and meaningful swing structure to judge whether a zone matters.
- Map nested premium and discount zones across timeframes without letting lower-timeframe noise rewrite the thesis.
- Build entries around explicit invalidation and risk instead of treating a zone as an automatic signal.

Audience: For price-action, SMC and ICT-style traders who want to use premium and discount as a disciplined location framework rather than as standalone reversal signals.

The Funded Trader Playbook reframes prop-firm trading as rule-constrained risk management rather than a race to hit a profit target. Daily loss, trailing drawdown, profit targets, trading targets and the failure boundary are translated into practical sizing and survival decisions.

Risk ladders, consecutive-loss planning, correlated exposure, session architecture, news restrictions and account-specific rules lead into psychology: target fixation, revenge trading and the temptation to accelerate after falling behind. - Build session and news rules that fit the firm's specific restrictions.
- Separate evaluation behavior from sustainable funded-account and payout behavior.

### The Heikin Ashi Trading Strategy

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/the-heikin-ashi-trading-strategy/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: A Practical Guide to Trend Reading, Transformed Candles, Entries, Risk, and Testing
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=KzQLEgAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=KzQLEgAAQBAJ&hl=en

The Heikin Ashi Trading Strategy explains the transformed candle series as a smoothing and trend-reading tool while keeping it separate from the actual prices available for execution. A Heikin Ashi close is not the market close, and a visually clean transformed sequence can hide the size and volatility of the underlying bars. Entry, stop and backtest rules therefore have to reference executable market prices rather than assume the transformed chart itself can be traded.

The book also explains why session gaps can appear reduced or disappear in Heikin Ashi even though real orders can still gap and slip. Trend persistence, trigger definitions, volatility, position sizing, exposure, trade frequency and drawdown are treated together so a visually elegant chart does not create false confidence about execution or risk.

Key topics: Heikin Ashi; Transformed candles; Trend persistence; Execution prices; Gap risk; Slippage; Volatility; Position sizing; Backtesting; Drawdown

What readers learn:
- Understand how Heikin Ashi values differ from ordinary OHLC market prices.
- Use transformed candles for trend description without pretending they are directly executable prices.
- Define entries and stops against actual market data when testing a Heikin Ashi strategy.
- Recognize that smoothed visual gaps do not remove real gap or slippage risk.
- Evaluate volatility, position size, trade frequency, exposure and drawdown alongside visual trend quality.

Audience: For traders who use Heikin Ashi charts and want to connect their visual clarity to realistic execution, risk and backtesting rules.

### The Mathematical Anatomy of Moving Averages:

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/the-mathematical-anatomy-of-moving-averages/
- Language: English

- DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21412298

The Mathematical Anatomy of Moving Averages treats a moving average as a model of market memory and a filter that estimates a slower market state rather than as a predictive line or guaranteed support level. Its 100-part architecture begins with foundations, then studies core moving averages, formulas, weights and failure modes before moving into advanced and adaptive smoothers, signal processing, statistical mathematics and parameter engineering.

The practical sections connect type, length, source and robustness to scalping, day trading, swing trading, position trading and market-specific applications. Each concept is designed around mathematical explanation, a worked market example, a key insight and an explicit limitation, ending with system design, validation and synthesis so indicator behavior is linked to assumptions, lag, noise and execution rather than reduced to simplistic crossover rules.

Key topics: Moving averages; SMA and EMA; Weighted averages; Adaptive smoothers; Signal processing; Statistical mathematics; Parameter engineering; Scalping and day trading; Swing and position trading; System validation

What readers learn:
- Understand what a moving average estimates and why smoothing necessarily trades responsiveness against noise.
- Compare formulas, weighting schemes, core averages and adaptive smoothers by their assumptions and failure modes.
- Connect moving averages to signal-processing and statistical ideas instead of treating them only as chart decorations.
- Engineer type, length and price source for different horizons including scalping, day trading, swing and position trading.
- Design and validate moving-average systems without presenting simulated examples or indicator lines as guaranteed market truth.

Audience: For technical and quantitative traders who want to understand moving averages mathematically, evaluate their limitations and use them more deliberately across trading horizons.

### The Wyckoff Method

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/the-wyckoff-method/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: A Practical Guide to Accumulation, Distribution, Springs, Upthrusts, and Market Structure

- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=nwgQEgAAQBAJ&hl=en

The Wyckoff Method is a working manual for reading ranges and transitions through evidence rather than memorizing an ideal accumulation or distribution schematic. It develops wave comparison, trend health, price-volume relationships, accumulation, distribution, springs, upthrusts, UTADs, reaccumulation, redistribution, structural failure, entry and risk while emphasizing what the market has actually demonstrated and what would invalidate the current hypothesis.

Progressive chart reveal, case studies, exercises, matrices and a visual appendix force the reader to make decisions before the right side of the chart is known. The closing CREST process—Context, Range, Evidence, Scenario, Trade or Stand Aside—compresses the method into a practical operating sequence. The recurring principle is evidence before labels, structure before prediction, and risk before conviction.

Key topics: Wyckoff Method; Accumulation; Distribution; Springs; Upthrusts and UTAD; Price and volume; Trading ranges; Reaccumulation; Redistribution; CREST decision map

What readers learn:
- Read accumulation and distribution as evolving evidence rather than fixed pictures.
- Interpret springs, upthrusts, reaccumulation and redistribution inside range context.
- Compare price, volume, waves and structural transitions without claiming certainty about hidden intent.
- Use progressive chart reveal and case studies to reduce hindsight bias.
- Apply the CREST decision sequence to context, range, evidence, scenario and the choice to trade or stand aside.

Audience: For serious beginners, intermediate discretionary traders, price-action and SMC traders, and stock, futures, forex or crypto traders who want a process-oriented framework for ranges and transitions.

### Turtle Soup Strategy

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/turtle-soup-strategy/
- Language: English
- Category: Trading
- Subtitle: The Turtle Soup Trading Strategy
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=KtsMEgAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=KtsMEgAAQBAJ&hl=en

Turtle Soup Strategy separates the historical failed-breakout idea from the modern vocabulary often layered on top of it. The classic architecture begins with a prior 20-period extreme, a fresh break beyond that boundary and a reclaim; a fresh break without reclaim is not the setup. The book also makes clear that Turtle Soup is not simply the original Turtle trend-following system run in reverse.

Modern terms such as liquidity sweep, market structure shift and Fair Value Gap are treated as later adaptations that should be tested separately rather than smuggled into the historical rule after losses. Daily, hourly and intraday use are compared with attention to the fact that the same 20-bar count represents very different market environments. Entries, invalidation, context, risk, replay and journaling preserve the setup as something that can actually be evaluated.

Key topics: Turtle Soup; Failed breakouts; 20-period highs and lows; Reclaim; Bullish Turtle Soup; Bearish Turtle Soup; Timeframe adaptation; Liquidity sweeps; Risk management; Backtesting

What readers learn:
- State the historical Turtle Soup sequence without mixing it with later SMC or ICT terminology.
- Identify the prior 20-period extreme, fresh break and reclaim that define the setup.
- Separate original rules from modern filters and test each version independently.
- Adapt the idea across daily and intraday timeframes without assuming a 20-bar lookback means the same thing everywhere.
- Use explicit invalidation, risk and journaling to evaluate failed breakouts honestly.

Audience: For reversal and breakout traders who want to understand the classic Turtle Soup framework, distinguish it from modern adaptations, and test it with clearer rules.

### Yapay Zekâ Çağında Etik

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/yapay-zeka-caginda-etik/
- Language: Turkish
- Category: Yapay Zekâ Etiği & Teknoloji
- Subtitle: Yapay Genel Zekâya Giden Yolda İnsan Sorumluluğu ve Doğru ile Yanlışın Yeni Sınırları
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=ne0UEgAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=ne0UEgAAQBAJ&hl=en

Yapay Zekâ Çağında Etik, yapay zekânın günlük yaşamdan eğitime, çalışma hayatından ilişkilere ve kamusal kararlara kadar giderek daha fazla alanı etkilediği bir dönemde doğru ile yanlışın sınırlarının nasıl yeniden tartışılması gerektiğini ele alır. Kitap, etik tartışmayı soyut ilkelerle sınırlamak yerine sorumluluk, mahremiyet, algoritmik ayrımcılık, gözetim, manipülasyon, deepfake'ler, açıklanabilirlik, belirsizlik ve insan denetimi gibi somut sorunlar üzerinden kurar.

Eser ayrıca otonom sistemler ve ajanlar, yapay genel zekâya giden yol, makine bilinci ve olası makine hakları gibi daha ileri tartışmalara uzanırken temel soruyu sürekli korur: karar verme yetkisi ve sonuçların sorumluluğu nerede insanda kalmalıdır? Eğitimde yapay zekâ kullanımı, iş ve becerilerin dönüşümü, ilişkiler, ebeveynlik, algoritmik eşleşme ve dijital yakınlık gibi gündelik konular da bu etik çerçevenin parçası olarak incelenir.

Kitabın yaklaşımı, teknolojiyi şeytanlaştırmak ya da romantikleştirmek yerine insan öznesini, hesap verebilirliği ve bilinçli gözetimi merkeze almaktır. Amaç, yapay zekâ ile birlikte yaşarken yalnızca neyin mümkün olduğunu değil, neyin kabul edilebilir, adil, sorumlu ve insan onuruyla uyumlu olduğunu da sorgulamaktır.

Key topics: Yapay zekâ etiği; İnsan sorumluluğu ve hesap verebilirlik; Algoritmik ayrımcılık ve adalet; Mahremiyet ve gözetim; Manipülasyon ve deepfake; Açıklanabilirlik ve şeffaflık; Belirsizlik ve karar verme; Bilişsel haklar ve insan özerkliği; Eğitimde yapay zekâ; İş, beceriler ve otomasyon; İlişkiler ve algoritmik eşleşme; Ebeveynlik ve dijital yaşam; Otonom ajanlar; Yapay Genel Zekâ (AGI); Makine bilinci ve olası makine hakları; İnsan denetimi ve yönetişim

What readers learn:
- Yapay zekâ sistemlerinde sorumluluğun neden yalnızca modele veya geliştiriciye indirgenemeyeceğini anlamak.
- Algoritmik ayrımcılık, mahremiyet, gözetim ve manipülasyon risklerini etik açıdan değerlendirmek.
- Deepfake, sentetik içerik ve ikna teknolojilerinin güven, kimlik ve kamusal alan üzerindeki etkilerini ayırt etmek.
- Açıklanabilirlik, şeffaflık ve belirsizliğin yüksek etkili yapay zekâ kararlarında neden önemli olduğunu görmek.
- Eğitim, iş, ilişkiler ve aile yaşamında yapay zekâ kullanımını insan özerkliği ve sorumluluk açısından sorgulamak.
- Otonom ajanlar ve yapay genel zekâya yaklaşırken yetki, denetim ve hesap verebilirlik sınırlarını düşünmek.
- Makine bilinci ve olası makine hakları tartışmalarını insan hakları ve etik sorumluluk çerçevesinde incelemek.
- Teknolojik kapasite ile etik kabul edilebilirlik arasındaki farkı koruyarak daha bilinçli kararlar vermek.

Audience: Yapay zekânın etik sonuçlarını anlamak isteyen öğrenciler, eğitimciler, geliştiriciler, araştırmacılar, yöneticiler, girişimciler, politika yapıcılar, teknoloji profesyonelleri ve günlük yaşamında yapay zekâ kullanan okurlar için hazırlanmıştır.

### İkinci Servet

- Canonical page: https://faramarzkowsari.github.io/books/ikinci-servet/
- Language: Türkçe
- Category: Yapay Zekâ, Kariyer Dönüşümü & Girişimcilik
- Subtitle: 50 Yaşından Sonra Yapay Zekâ ile Gelir Oluşturmanın Uygulamalı Rehberi
- Google Books: https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=mc78EQAAQBAJ
- Preview: https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=mc78EQAAQBAJ&hl=en

İkinci Servet, yıllar içinde birikmiş muhakeme, bilgi, ilişki, itibar ve örüntü tanıma becerisini modern yapay zekâ araçlarıyla hizmete, ürüne ve sisteme dönüştürmek isteyen deneyimli yetişkinler için uygulamalı bir rehberdir. Kitap hızlı zenginlik vaadi sunmaz; önce zaman ve para pistini, kullanılabilir deneyimi, üretken yapay zekânın sınırlarını, pazar seçimini, mahremiyeti ve kanıt disiplinini kurar. Ardından pahalı sorunları bulma, müşteriyle konuşma, yol seçimi, platform işi, paketli hizmet, işletme değerlendirmesi, dijital varlık, mikro araç, fiyatlandırma, ilk yirmi kapı, keşif görüşmeleri, SOP, kanıttan sonra otomasyon ve sahip olunan varlıklara geçiş üzerinde ilerler. Beşinci bölümde hizmet, yazı ve editörlük, yerel işletme içeriği, açılış sayfası, AI fırsat değerlendirmesi, dijital ürün, içerik motoru ve tek işlevli araç laboratuvarları vardır. Son doksan günlük plan seçimden örnek üretmeye, pazara çıkmaya, ilk teslimata, süreci belgelemeye ve tekrar edilebilir bir gelir sistemine doğru ilerler. Uygulama ekleri; hazırlık testleri, deneyim envanteri, sorun puan kartı, müşteri görüşmesi, teklif kartı, fiyatlandırma, mesaj örnekleri, teklif ve SOP şablonları, mahremiyet kontrolü ve doksan günlük panel sağlar.

Key topics: 50 yaşından sonra AI ile gelir; Deneyim sermayesi ve muhakeme; Kariyer dönüşümü; Zaman ve para pisti; ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini ve Notebook; Brief yazımı ve doğrulanabilir araştırma; Mahremiyet ve veri sınırları; Müşteri keşfi; Pahalı sorunlar ve pazar doğrulama; Platform işleri; Paketli hizmetler; AI fırsat değerlendirmesi; Dijital ürünler ve mikro araçlar; Fiyatlandırma ve sınırlar; Müşteri erişimi ve keşif görüşmeleri; SOP ve kanıttan sonra otomasyon; Sahip olunan varlıklar ve dayanıklılık; 90 günlük kanıt planı

What readers learn:
- Deneyim, muhakeme, ilişki ve örüntü tanıma içinde saklı ekonomik değeri görünür kılmak.
- Bir gelir yolunu seçmeden önce gerçekçi zaman, para ve enerji pistini hesaplamak.
- Üretken yapay zekâyı denetlenmesi gereken hızlı bir çırak gibi kullanmak.
- Müşteri görüşmeleri, sinyaller ve kanıtla bir pazar ve değerli sorun seçmek.
- Deneyimi paketli hizmete, değerlendirmeye, dijital varlığa, içerik sistemine veya küçük araca dönüştürmek.
- Fiyat, kapsam, mahremiyet, insan onayı ve başarı ölçüsünü otomasyondan önce tanımlamak.
- Örnekler, erişim mesajları, keşif görüşmeleri ve pilotlarla gerçek talebi test etmek.
- Tekrarlanabilir teslimi belgelemek ve yalnız kanıtlandıktan sonra düşük riskli otomasyon kurmak.
- Doksan günlük plan ve uygulama ekleriyle öğrenmeyi dış dünyada ölçülebilir kanıta çevirmek.

Audience: Deneyimli profesyoneller, emekliler, kariyer değiştirenler, danışmanlar, yöneticiler, eğitmenler ve 50 yaş üstünde yılların deneyimini yapay zekâ araçlarıyla gerçekçi ve kanıta dayalı bir ikinci gelir sistemine dönüştürmek isteyen okurlar için.
